items.title: Microscopic origin of exceptional superconducting interfaces in molybdenum-rhenium contacts
items.original_title: Exceptional Superconducting Interfaces between Graphene and Atomic Chains in A15-MoRe
authors: Hiroto Ogura, Yuto Tsukidate, Shun Kondo, Zhuoqun Li, Natsuki Sasaki, Tsunenobu Sato, Azusa Utsumi, Tomohiro Otsuka, Mitsuhiro Saito, Kazutoshi Inoue, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Yuichi Ikuhara, Toshiaki Kato
items.continuity_note: Not included in the recent archived briefings.
items.summary: Molybdenum-rhenium alloys provide ballistic, highly transparent contacts to two-dimensional materials, but the microscopic origin of this behavior has remained unclear. By combining low-temperature transport, X-ray diffraction, and electron microscopy, researchers discovered that as-deposited contacts spontaneously form a classical A15 superconducting phase. The one-dimensional transition-metal atomic chains within this phase exhibit a near-perfect lattice match with graphene edges.
items.why: Understanding this interface structure establishes A15-phase superconductors as a geometrically ideal platform for developing robust quantum electronics.
technical_details: Thermal annealing triggers a phase transition to a hexagonal close-packed structure that degrades Josephson transparency, while A15 d-orbitals may hybridize with graphene's Dirac cone.
items.selection_reason: Resolves the mechanism behind transparent superconducting contacts between MoRe and graphene via 1D atomic chains.
items.corroboration: Single substantive source; independent corroboration not established.
items.display_title: Microscopic origin of exceptional superconducting interfaces in molybdenum-rhenium contacts

items.title: New Adaptive Optics Method Improves Deep Tissue Nanoscale Imaging and Fabrication
items.original_title: Focal-Plane Extreme Adaptive Optics for Deep Super Resolution Imaging and Nanolithography
authors: Jinxin Liu, Jiahao Niu, Runxin Zeng, Kaining Yang, Ziyu Li, Xiaodong Guan, Jing Ren, Kebin Shi, Yue Wang, Shan Zhao, Yujie Sun, He Sun
items.continuity_note: Not included in the recent archived briefings.
items.summary: Researchers have introduced a technique called focal-plane extreme adaptive optics to overcome optical aberrations in heterogeneous media at significant depths. The approach directly controls the terminal focal-plane complex field using cascaded deformable mirrors and closed-form control. In testing, the method maintained high localization precision at deep tissue levels and reduced minimum written linewidths in photoresist during nanolithography.
items.why: This optical advancement significantly extends the depth and speed limits for high-resolution biological imaging and nanoscale optical writing.
technical_details: Achieved imaging to 160 um depth in brain tissue with approximately 18 nm localization precision.
Reduced minimum written linewidth to 88.8 nm at 160 um depth in photoresist during STED nanolithography.
items.selection_reason: Introduces focal-plane extreme adaptive optics (FP-ExAO) to drastically improve super-resolution imaging and nanolithography depth performance and linewidth reduction.
items.corroboration: Single substantive source; independent corroboration not established.
items.display_title: New Adaptive Optics Method Improves Deep Tissue Nanoscale Imaging and Fabrication

items.title: Mistral releases open weights for trillion-parameter cybersecurity artificial intelligence model
items.original_title: Mistral releases weights for its trillion-parameter AI model, targeting cybersecurity
items.continuity_note: Not included in the recent archived briefings.
items.summary: French artificial intelligence company Mistral has released the numerical training parameters for its large-scale open-weight model, Mistral Large 4, allowing organizations to download and run the system locally. Nicknamed "Le Chonk," the trillion-parameter model is designed to give enterprises and government agencies direct control over advanced cyber defense infrastructure without relying on outside providers. The developers report that the system achieves high-level performance while using fewer computational tokens per task than certain competing open-weight models.
items.why: Releasing these model weights gives enterprises and government agencies sovereign control over advanced cybersecurity tools, preventing external providers from cutting off access during critical security incidents.
technical_details: The model uses 47 percent fewer tokens per task compared to the competing open-weight model GLM-5.3.
Mistral states the model leads open models on Artificial Analysis' Coding Agent Index for agentic coding tasks.
items.selection_reason: Mistral releases weights for its trillion-parameter open-weight model, marking a significant development in open-source AI infrastructure.
items.corroboration: Single substantive source; independent corroboration not established.
items.display_title: Mistral releases open weights for trillion-parameter cybersecurity artificial intelligence model

items.title: High-Fidelity Spin Qubit Control in Industrial Silicon Wafers
items.original_title: High-fidelity qubit control in a natural Si-MOS quantum dot using a 300 mm silicon on insulator wafer
items.continuity_note: No material new development could be established from available evidence.
items.summary: Researchers have demonstrated high-fidelity single qubit control using electron spin resonance in a natural silicon metal-oxide-semiconductor quantum dot. The device was fabricated using an industrial 300-millimeter wafer process on a silicon-on-insulator substrate. Feedback protocols and a fast Rabi frequency helped mitigate low-frequency magnetic noise from the environment.
items.why: Demonstrating high gate fidelity in industrial silicon manufacturing processes supports the scalable development of silicon-based quantum processors.
technical_details: Randomized benchmarking yielded an average single gate control fidelity of 99.5 percent, with Q-factors exceeding 50 at an optimal Rabi frequency of 5 megahertz.
items.selection_reason: Demonstrates high-fidelity single qubit control in a natural Si-MOS quantum dot using a 300 mm industrial wafer process.
items.corroboration: Single substantive source; independent corroboration not established.
items.display_title: High-Fidelity Spin Qubit Control in Industrial Silicon Wafers
